goal: Teach frontend-oriented AEM developers how editable templates define the authoring contract for pages, while separating template type, structure, initial content, policy and page-owned content by lifecycle.

deck_context.source_summary: Class 6 of a seven-week AEM Sites course, delivered Monday, August 24, 2026. The audience already understands JCR Resources, repository boundaries and Sling request resolution. This class begins Week 2 and prepares the individual Guide Page authoring practice.
deck_context.core_claim: A reliable AEM authoring contract places shared structure, creation-time defaults, design policy and page-owned content in different repository branches according to ownership and synchronization behavior.
canonical_facts: Page content lives below /content and a page jcr:content Resource can store both cq:template and sling:resourceType.
cq:template records the editable template; sling:resourceType selects the page component used for rendering.
A template type is copied when an editable template is created; the remaining reference is informational rather than dynamic inheritance.
Structure changes remain connected to pages created from the template.
Initial content is copied when a page is created and later initial-content changes do not update existing pages.
Policies define design and authoring rules and are explored in Day 7.

slides.intent: Show which editable-template changes continue to affect existing pages.

Later structure changes are reflected on existing pages

slides.title: Initial content is copied only when the page is created.
slides.intent: Prevent initial content from being mistaken for synchronization or migration.

Authors can edit or remove eligible copied content
Changing initial content affects future pages, not existing pages
Existing content needs an explicit migration

slides.title: Key takeaways
slides.intent: Retrieve the five distinctions needed before beginning the Guide Page practice.
key_points: The page stores content; the page component renders it
